policy_title:
Lung Cancer Screening with Low Dose
Computed Tomography (LDCT)

reimbursement_guidelines.title: Reimbursement Guidelines
reimbursement_guidelines.content:
ABH IL will only reimburse for prostate cancer screening when appropriately reported. 
Appropriate reporting includes 
• 
Reporting the screening CPT code or counseling HCPCS code for patients 50 years of age 
or older 
• 
Reporting the screening CPT code or counseling HCPCS code with a diagnosis indicating 
nicotine dependence 
• 
Reporting the screening CPT code no more than once per year by any provider 
 
Claims that are submitted will be denied when 
• 
The screening CPT code or counseling HCPCS code is reported for patients 49 years of 
age or younger 
• 
The screening CPT code or counseling HCPCS code is not reported with a diagnosis 
indicating nicotine dependence 
• 
The screening CPT code is reported more than once per year by any provider 
 
The medical record documentation is expected to support the specific CPT, HCPCS code(s), 
ICD-10-CM codes and modifiers reported.

This policy outlines the coding and editing guidelines for reporting Lung Cancer Screening with 
Low Dose Computed Tomography (LDCT). Lung cancer detection and treatment at an early 
stage is important for improving survival rates. A common method used for detection is LDCT, 
also known as spiral or helical CT scanning which provides high quality, three-dimensional 
images of the lungs during a single breath to identify the presence of lung cancer in an individual 
that does not demonstrate any symptoms. This policy applies to all professional and facility claim 
types. 
 
Screening Limitations 
LDCT and related counseling services to discuss the need for screening are considered 
appropriate for patients aged 50 or older and should be reported with an applicable ICD-10-CM 
diagnosis code that indicates nicotine dependence. Services reported for patients under the age 
of 50 or reported without a nicotine dependence-related diagnosis code will be denied. 
 
When an LDCT screening is indicated, it should not be performed more than once within a 12-
month period (where are least 11 full months have passed) by any provider. Screenings that are 
conducted more than one within a 12-month period by any provider will be denied.

Applicable CPT Code 
71271 
Computed tomography, thorax, low dose for lung cancer screening, without 
contrast material(s) 
 
Applicable HCPCS Code 
G0296 
Counseling visit to discuss need for lung cancer screening using low dose 
CT scan (LDCT) 
 
Applicable ICD-10-CM Diagnosis Code 
F17.21X 
Nicotine dependence, cigarettes 
F17.29X 
Nicotine Dependence 
Z12.2 
Encounter for screening for malignant neoplasm of respiratory organs 
Z72.0 
Tobacco Use 
Z87.891 
Personal history of nicotine dependence

A medical code set maintained by the American Medical
Association through the CPT Editorial Panel. The CPT code set
(copyright protected by the AMA) describes medical, surgical,
and diagnostic services and is designed to communicate uniform
information about medical services and procedures among
physicians, coders, patients, accreditation organizations, and
payers for administrative, financial, and analytical purposes.

Level II of the HCPCS is a standardized coding system that is used
primarily to identify products, supplies, and services not included
in the CPT code set. Examples include ambulance services and
durable medical equipment, prosthetics, orthotics, and supplies
(DMEPOS). Level II HCPCS codes were established to allow these
products, supplies and services to be reported for
reimbursement.
